key_insight: The Nephro Candidate Score (N-CS) uses machine learning to rank genes and variants that may explain suspected inherited kidney disease, helping surface plausible disease candidates from large sequencing datasets.
clinical_relevance: This tool could speed up interpretation of exome data in patients with suspected genetic kidney disease and support more standardized candidate variant prioritization in research and diagnostic workflows.
method: Combines a Nephro Gene Score, Nephro Variant Score, and an inheritance-based heuristic into one prioritization framework.
Uses XGBoost to estimate gene-disease relevance and logistic regression to estimate variant pathogenicity from genomic features.
Evaluated with exome-wide candidate discovery, gene-level burden analysis, and external validation against newly proposed kidney disease genes.
evidence_signal: In independent test sets, the N-GS achieved AUC 0.94 and the N-VS achieved AUC 0.99, with enrichment of kidney-related pathways among top-ranked genes and high scores for 10 of 11 external candidate genes.
watch_item: Performance was shown in retrospective and validation datasets, so prospective clinical impact and generalizability across diverse populations and sequencing pipelines still need confirmation.
paper_title: Automated Variant Prioritization in Suspected Genetic Kidney Disease
